reason: Both updates target a real, reproducible failure in the current batch: P1/P3/P6 all burn the budget cycling among closed cabinets/drawers while reachable surface and appliance receptacles go uninspected. I keep the direction of both requirements but repair two defects exposed by the evidence and by Actor capabilities. First, u1's 'prefer a candidate you have not yet observed' and u2's 'remaining untested receptacles' presuppose a full visited-set, which the Actor cannot maintain (only the last two pre-action observations are available); I replace these with concrete, locally observable triggers. Second, memory M6/M3 show that prior anti-cycling/'complete a first pass' wording was repeatedly not followed and did not break the cycling mode, so I do not simply repeat it more strongly; I replace u2 with an executable two-step-window loop-breaker plus a same-type-to-surface switch, flagged as an unverified exploration hypothesis. u1's overgeneral 'targets are frequently placed plainly visible' is softened to an evidence-grounded 'often' and reframed as an early, cheap surface/appliance pass. The desklamp procedure and general exact-target/clean/place behavior are untouched.

+ When the exact requested target is not visible at the start, broaden the search beyond closed cabinets and drawers to open surfaces and appliances, because a target is often plainly visible there: check coffeetable, diningtable, sidetable, dresser top, countertop, sofa, armchair, and ottoman, and appliances such as fridge, microwave, stoveburner, sinkbasin, toaster, and coffeemachine.
+ Because arriving at an already-open surface reveals its contents immediately, make one early pass over these open surfaces and appliances as soon as the target is not found in the first closed container or two, rather than spending the budget re-opening the same cabinets and drawers while surface and appliance locations from the command list remain unvisited; inspect each receptacle you reach on first arrival (open it and read its contents).
+ Continue this first pass until the exact target, or the required number of target instances for a multi-target task, is located, or until all reachable candidate receptacles have been inspected once.

adjustments.reason: P1 cycled through closed cabinets/drawers and only reached coffeetable 1, where the requested box was plainly visible, at step 36 (P1:36-37), after roughly 35 container steps. P6 inspected drawers, sidetables, and the dresser but never visited the diningtable, ottoman, or sofa that its own command list offered (C61), and hit the step limit (P6:outcome). This supports broadening to open surfaces and appliances. I softened the old 'targets are frequently placed plainly visible' universal claim to 'often' and reframed the instruction as an early, cheap pass because arrival at an open surface immediately reveals contents. I also removed 'prefer a candidate you have not yet observed', which requires tracking every seen receptacle that the Actor cannot do with only the last two observations, and replaced it with the observable criterion 'while surface/appliance locations from the command list remain unvisited'. Memory M6 shows broader search helped in some cases (a diningtable bread find) but was not reliably followed, so this is a supported direction, not a guaranteed benefit.

to.patch:
--- a/SKILL.md
+++ b/SKILL.md
@@ -1,3 +1,3 @@
- After inspecting a receptacle that visibly lacks the exact target, do not re-open or re-walk a receptacle you have already confirmed empty; next travel to a receptacle that does not appear in your recent observation/action history and whose contents you have not yet seen.
- Do not cycle back and forth among the same small set of receptacles; before making any second pass over a container cluster, complete one inspection of the remaining untested receptacle types or instances.
- Treat a run of steps that only revisits already-open, empty containers as a stuck-search signal: break the pattern by moving to an uninspected surface or appliance instead of repeating the loop.
+ Use the current observation and the last two action/observation pairs to avoid looping: when you arrive at a receptacle that is already open and shows it contains nothing, do not linger there or immediately return to it; pick a different destination from the command list instead.
+ If your most recent moves have been among the same closed-container type (for example several drawers or several cabinets) without finding the exact target, treat that as a stuck signal: your next move must be to a surface or appliance receptacle from the command list that you have not just checked, not another container of the same type.
+ Do not move to an unrelated location or treat the search as finished while the exact target is still unfound and untried surface or appliance locations remain in the command list; make one inspection pass over the remaining candidate receptacles before any second visit.

adjustments.reason: All three runs exhibit the cycling the goal targets: P1 revisits opened empty cabinets/drawers (P1:15, P1:20), P3 loops among the same cabinets (P3:9 and repeated first-pass cycles to the limit), and P6 shuttles among drawers 1-4 and the dresser to the step limit (P6:7, P6:26, P6:outcome). But the original wording relies on 'remaining untested receptacles', i.e., a visited-set the Actor cannot keep with only two-step history, and memory M6/M3 record that prior 'do not re-walk / complete a first pass' language was not reliably followed and did not break the mode. Rather than repeat it more forcefully, I replace it with an executable local loop-breaker: use the two-step window and the command list, leave an already-open empty receptacle at once, and after two fruitless same-type container moves switch to a different receptacle type. This is an unverified exploration hypothesis with an observable trigger and falsifiable expectation (the check), not a proven fix.
